items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Henry Martin was one of the best.

ctx.x: On the snare drum. On the street.

Them times? Mm-hmm. I'll tell you. Henry Martin was one of the best. Mm-hmm. Well, Happy, I don't believe I've never seen him play. Yeah, I did see him play parade. He played parade with us once. Long time ago. He played nice. I had Black Benny on the bass drum. He's the bad man on the bass drum. Boy, he played more bass drum. Sure.
Now, back to the piano players. What about Manuel Bonetta? Did you ever work with him?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: But it started by Henry Martin and Black Bennett. They didn't want to start that. They just told us to light out on the blues and we did it.

ctx.x: Oh, sure. All the time. Two or three times, sometimes. Mm-hmm.
But it started by Henry Martin and Black Bennett. They didn't want to start that. They just told us to light out on the blues and we did it. Who else was in that band?
We got the trumpets and the drums.
Oh, that's Aureus drummer, Henry Martin. That's the same guy?
